label: Merge
description: Katie Crutchfield's fifth Waxahatchee album traded her indie-rock guitars for a warmer, twangier palette of pedal steel and loping tempos, written in the wake of getting sober. The plainspoken lyrics about family, memory and the South landed it a Best Americana Album Grammy nomination and a Libera Award for Best Country Record. It is the record most often cited as the moment 'indie twang' became a recognizable Bandcamp-to-country pipeline.
lineage: Grows out of Crutchfield's earlier lo-fi indie-rock work into full country songwriting, directly inspiring the Plains project with Jess Williamson and a wave of indie musicians (MJ Lenderman among them) leaning into twang.

label: Anti-
description: Waxahatchee's sixth album deepens the country turn of Saint Cloud with a full touring band feel, harmonies from MJ Lenderman, and some of Crutchfield's most direct, hook-driven songwriting. Critics called it the decade's most fitting songwriter pivot, and it earned a Grammy nomination for Best Americana Album. It is a good entry point for the wider Bandcamp-to-country scene the record helped popularize.
lineage: A continuation of the country-facing sound Crutchfield established on Saint Cloud, cementing the connection between the Waxahatchee/Plains circle and the Asheville MJ Lenderman scene.

album: I Walked with You a Ways
label: Anti-
description: A one-off duo album pairing Katie Crutchfield (Waxahatchee) with fellow songwriter Jess Williamson, built around plush '90s-country vocal harmonies and pedal steel over breakup-and-friendship songs. It plays like a loving homage to Lucinda Williams and Trisha Yearwood-style country radio filtered through two indie songwriters. A key document of the indie scene's mid-2020s country turn.
lineage: A direct collaborative offshoot of Waxahatchee's country pivot, pairing Crutchfield with Jess Williamson's own move from folk toward country songwriting.

label: Self-released
description: Aaron Dowdy's self-released full-length debut as Fust is a lo-fi, plainspoken alt-country record built from years of home-recorded songs, its narrators drifting through small Southern towns and bad decisions. It set the template the band expanded on with a full lineup on Genevieve and Big Ugly. A quieter, more private-sounding entry point into the band's catalog.
lineage: Fust's founding document, growing out of Dowdy's earlier self-released EPs into the fuller alt-country sound the band pursued once signed to Dear Life Records.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Fust's Dear Life Records debut fills out Aaron Dowdy's plainspoken songwriting with a full band, landing on Pitchfork's list of albums you should be listening to. The songs mix wry, character-driven storytelling with a loose, unhurried alt-country backing. It is the record that put the Durham band on the national indie-country radar.
lineage: Expands Evil Joy's lo-fi songwriting into a fuller band sound after signing to Dear Life Records, setting up the more widely reviewed Big Ugly.

label: Dear Life Records
description: Fust's third album is a detail-rich, character-driven record about visiting a grandmother's childhood Appalachian neighborhood, cut with help from Alex Farrar and members of Sluice. It landed on year-end lists from Time, Paste and NPR and got the band a CBS Saturday Morning performance slot. The most widely acclaimed entry in the band's catalog to date.
lineage: Continues Fust's Dear Life Records run, cementing the North Carolina country-textured songwriting line that runs alongside Wednesday and MJ Lenderman's Asheville-adjacent scene.

label: Self-released
description: The Chicago band's debut mixes cosmic country and psychedelic choogle with straight honky-tonk, split between co-lead singers Chris Coleslaw and Lexi Goddard, and drew praise from NPR and Rolling Stone. Pedal steel and reverb-soaked guitars sit under barroom, heartbreak-and-hangover songwriting. A stellar, unpolished debut that established the band's neon-lit small-hours sound.
lineage: Draws on classic honky-tonk duet singing and cosmic country in the Gram Parsons/Emmylou Harris mold, feeding directly into the band's more widely reviewed follow-up Horses.
borderline_note: Terry's post describes this as a 2021 LP, but the Bandcamp page states it was released January 30, 2023; used the scraped release date.

label: Self-released
description: Tobacco City's second album widens their neon-lit country sound with more players (violin, hammered dulcimer, extra keys) while keeping the boozy small-town nostalgia of their debut. It channels '70s country touchstones like Gram Parsons while singing about smoking behind the grocery store and gas-station romance. A confident, more fully arranged follow-up to Tobacco City, USA.
lineage: A direct sequel to Tobacco City, USA, expanding the same Chicago cosmic-country lineup with more collaborators from the city's alt-country scene.

label: Ever/Never Records
description: Chicago's National Photo Committee plays raucous, country-tinged bar rock, with spidery pedal steel lines cutting through gravelly, shouted vocals. Its songs favor an unresisting, rowdy energy over polish, closer to a loud honky-tonk stage than a studio. A record built to be heard live.
lineage: Part of the same Chicago DIY-country circle as Tobacco City and Red PK, connecting the city's cowpunk-adjacent bar-rock scene to the wider Bandcamp alt-country revival.

label: Self-released
description: Chicago songwriter Andy 'Red' PK (also the pedal steel player in Tobacco City) makes hushed, banjo-and-pedal-steel folk-country under his own name, backed by players from the city's DIY scene. The songs are intimate and unshowy, closer to a bedroom recording than a full-band statement. Part of the same small Chicago country circle as Tobacco City and National Photo Committee.
lineage: Grows directly out of the Chicago alt-country scene centered on Tobacco City, where PK also plays pedal steel.

label: Sophomore Lounge
description: Kentucky songwriter Grace Rogers' debut LP puts conversational, character-based storytelling over jangly electric guitar and a friendly, unpolished full-band sound, cut at Louisville's End of an Ear studio. Her lyrics draw on family stories from her home region (a rabid-dog outbreak, a fiddling great-grandfather) with a poet's eye for detail. A warm, inviting entry point into the Louisville indie-country scene around Sophomore Lounge.
lineage: Comes out of the same Louisville scene as Ryan Davis & the Roadhouse Band and Sophomore Lounge's country-adjacent roster, rooted in Rogers' own old-time and string-band family background.

label: Self-released
description: Tulsa songwriter Ken Pomeroy's breakout album is a stripped-back, autobiographical collection of contemporary folk-country, drawing on her Cherokee heritage and coming-of-age stories with sophisticated vocal harmonies. It won her attention from John Moreland and Reservation Dogs' Sterlin Harjo before a string of high-profile 2025/2026 tour dates. A brutally honest, unshowy record built around voice and guitar.
lineage: Sits alongside the Oklahoma/Texas red-dirt songwriter tradition, sharing an audience with the Sturgill Simpson/outlaw-adjacent wing of the new country scene.

label: Rounder Records
description: Calgary-born, bluegrass-trained singer Bella White's sophomore album pairs jaw-dropping opening lines about moving on with mesmerizing, Appalachian-rooted picking, produced by Jonathan Wilson. It widens her sound with country, indie and classic-rock textures without losing the traditional bluegrass core. A striking, introspective record from one of the scene's most technically accomplished young singers.
lineage: Extends the Appalachian bluegrass tradition through a Canadian songwriter's lens, part of the same young-traditionalist wave as Bella White's Rounder Records labelmates.

label: New West Records
description: Nenni's third album widens her honky-tonk base with Memphis and Muscle Shoals soul horns and organ, again produced by John James Tourville, while keeping her focus on the dancefloor as a place of escape and self-acceptance. The songwriting turns more explicitly toward self-forgiveness and imperfection. A fuller, more soul-inflected step from her earlier records.
lineage: Extends Nenni's honky-tonk catalog toward Southern soul, echoing the same rock-and-soul crossover Margo Price and Jaime Wyatt have pursued on their later albums.

album: JP Harris Is a Trash Fire
label: Bloodshot Records
description: Nashville honky-tonker and clawhammer banjoist JP Harris' Bloodshot Records debut under his own name is self-aware, satirical country songwriting, gutting and funny often in the same verse. It marks a shift from his earlier old-time and bluegrass side projects toward a more pointed, personal honky-tonk voice. Praised for lyrics that are as decent as they are cutting.
lineage: Follows Harris's years fronting JP Harris and the Tough Choices and his old-time Dreadful Wind and Rain project, landing him on Bloodshot's classic insurgent-country roster.

label: Verve Forecast Records
description: Kentucky songwriter S.G. Goodman's debut is a rocking, rootsy country-folk record steeped in her rural western-Kentucky upbringing, connected with My Morning Jacket's Jim James, who produced it. Tyler Childers later covered its song 'Space and Time.' A stark, plainspoken start to Goodman's catalog.
lineage: Sits alongside Tyler Childers and Ian Noe in the western-Kentucky storyteller wing of the new country scene, sharing Childers' own admiration and later cover of her material.

label: Verve Forecast Records
description: Goodman's second album sharpens her rural-Kentucky storytelling into a bleaker, more electric record about depression and rural isolation, earning her the Americana Music Association's Emerging Artist of the Year award. The arrangements lean harder into fuzzy guitar than her debut without losing its plainspoken drawl. A more confident, harder-hitting follow-up.
lineage: Extends Old Time Feeling's western-Kentucky storytelling into darker territory, part of the same post-Childers Kentucky scene as Ian Noe.
key_tracks: All My Love Is Coming Back to Me

label: Slough Water Records
description: Goodman's third album, released on her own Slough Water Records with Thirty Tigers, turns toward the folk-magic and planting traditions of her rural Kentucky community for its imagery. It keeps the plainspoken, rootsy sound of her earlier records while widening its spiritual and agricultural language. A settled, personal record from one of the scene's most distinctive Kentucky voices.
lineage: Continues Goodman's western-Kentucky storytelling lineage on her own label imprint, tying her catalog directly to the region's folk traditions.

label: New West Records
description: Hedley's third album keeps building on his throwback Nashville-Sound sound with New West, continuing the honky-tonk revivalism of Neon Blue. It is the most recent entry in a catalog built entirely around classic-country authenticity rather than novelty. A steady, dependable extension of his sound.
lineage: Extends Hedley's classic-country throwback catalog for a third record on New West Records.

label: La Honda Records / RCA Records
description: Emerson's fourth album continues his La Honda/RCA run, extending the fuller country-rock sound of The Golden Crystal Kingdom. It keeps his East Texas storytelling focus while showing a still-expanding sonic palette. The most recent entry in his fast-growing catalog.
lineage: Continues Emerson's La Honda/RCA-era country-rock sound, extending the same Texas songwriter lineage as his earlier records.

label: Merge Records
description: Case Oats' debut album, led by singer Casey Gomez Walker and featuring Spencer Tweedy on drums, is a remarkably assured set of character studies drawn from Walker's creative-writing background, backed by pedal steel and fiddle. It moves easily between confessional-poem weight and conversational ease. A confident debut from a young Chicago band with deep Wilco-adjacent connections.
lineage: Grows out of Chicago's indie-country circle around Spencer Tweedy and Merge Records, connecting to the wider Waxahatchee/MJ Lenderman scene the label also releases.

label: Self-released
description: Chicago-by-way-of-Minnesota songwriter Tommy Goodroad's debut studio album mixes Midwestern folksy roots music with rollicking classic honky-tonk, co-produced by Amos Pitsch (Tenement, Hotline TNT). Backed by his touring band the Highway Birds, it leans on fiddle and pedal steel over a rowdy country-rock backbone. A confident full-band debut after years of live shows.
lineage: Part of the same Chicago DIY-country network as Case Oats and Tobacco City, blending Midwestern roots music with classic honky-tonk and outlaw touches.

label: Self-released
description: Nashville-based, Indiana-raised Kiely Connell's debut record is sparse, unburdened alt-country songwriting named for the Calumet River near her hometown of Hammond, Indiana. The arrangements stay spare and intimate, built to foreground her plainspoken, unsettled lyrics. A quietly confident debut steeped in Midwestern small-town detail.
lineage: A Midwestern-to-Nashville songwriter story typical of the current alt-country scene, sharing an audience and touring circuit with Tommy Goodroad and other Chicago-area acts.
borderline_note: Terry's list names a 2024 album 'My Own Company' by Kiely Connell that could not be located on her Bandcamp page (which calls Calumet Queen her debut); sent to needs_verification.

label: Self-released
description: Blue County Pistol's five-song EP is a rollicking, banjo-heavy alt-country release, warm and instantly familiar in its melodies. It plays like a tight, focused introduction rather than a sprawling statement. A small but well-loved entry in the Bandcamp alt-country underground.
lineage: Part of the wider Bandcamp-driven alt-country underground, sharing the banjo-and-drawl approach of countless small self-released country EPs of the early 2020s.

label: Anti-
description: Nashville songwriter Brennan Wedl's self-titled debut full-length, co-produced by Katie Crutchfield and Brad Cook with backing from Waxahatchee/Snocaps players Colin Croom and Matt McCaughan, blends arena-scaled country-rock hooks with swaggering, confessional lyrics. It moves between honky-tonk pastiche ('Fake Cowboy') and glammy indie-rock without losing its country backbone. A confident debut announcing a direct link to the Waxahatchee circle.
lineage: A direct extension of the Waxahatchee/Katie Crutchfield production circle (also behind Snocaps and MJ Lenderman), bringing Wedl into the same Anti- Records country-adjacent roster.
